designs.title: Engine A v4x: cut the v4 / v4c fixed cost at T = 2..256 (stream-K tickets deferred to one end-of-CTA round, warp-parallel pass list, 32-bit split, gs in smem). Bitwise twins raced per class: moe first, then decode classes 8/16/32 and the T=128/256 cold half
designs.summary:
Engine A v4 / v4c costs about 20-21 us per call on the H200 at T = 2..32, plus 7.34 us per pass. The decode cold half at T = 128/256 costs 27.4 + 7.34·k_c us. The empty-launch floor is 9.3 us, and the marginal pass already runs at 88% of the 4.37 TB/s ring. So the lever at these T is the fixed cost, not streaming.

The per-PC anatomy and the H100 staircase locate that fixed cost:
- P3b (H100 ncu): consumer.fixup is 11.6/15.2/17.0% of v4 samples, MEMBAR 6.7-9.7%, and build_map behind thread 0's serial pass loop 4.3-10.4%.
- K9 (H100 staircase): every aligned→stream-K onset adds +4.5-6.6 us over the normal per-expert step (T=8 4→5: +15.4/+16.2 vs 9.6; 8→9: +11.2..+14.5 vs 9.5).
- On the H200, the one decode cold-half draw whose K2 runs aligned (k_c=8) sits 8.6 us under the 23-point fit.

v4x keeps the stream-K decomposition, the ring, the consume code, the slots, the contributor set and the CTA-ordered fp32 sum. It changes four things:
1. Partial super-groups only publish mid-stream (no fence, barrier or ticket). Each CTA does one ticket round at its end: bar, thread 0 does fence.acq_rel + ≤2 relaxed atomics + fence.acq_rel, bar. The last arriver finishes with batched __ldcg loads. This is the CUTLASS GenericBarrier ordering, and the same pattern already passed on the judge in bf16's split-K ticket.
2. Warp 0 builds the pass list and v4c's prefix costs with lane-per-expert scans.
3. The split math is 32-bit, exact within static bounds.
4. gs is preloaded into smem.

The outputs are bitwise identical to v4 / v4c. A CPU emulator proves the map, split and protocol equivalence; on the judge, a NaN-poisoned bitwise canary checks the kernel's own output against the incumbent's.

Plan:
- **Stage 1:** the kernel plus moe races at classes 8/16/32 and T=128 (about 3 h).
- **Stage 2:** the decode port (classes 8/16/32 and the 128/256 cold halves).
- **Stage 3:** re-race the big-T work split.
- **Stage 4:** an early-combine twin.

Expected gains:
- **moe:** +3.3% (range 2.0-4.6%): verify 1 84.8→~79.8, decode 16 109.7→~103.2, decode 32 149.2→~142.7, verify 16 238.1→~231.6 us.
- **decode:** +1.8% (range 1.1-2.7%).

Both depend on tonight's prepare-only staircase checks (TC1 moe, TC2 decode). They measure the H200 stream-K onset excess with today's kernels and decide whether the ticket change is built.

stages.name: S1: v4x kernel + moe twin races (T=2..8, 9..16, 17..32, 128)
stages.milestone:
From one moe check:
- **[ea4x] build:** K1x and K2x at 0 lmem, ≤ 112 regs, 2 CTAs/SM.
- **Canary:** bitwise equal to v4 / v4c on every input, both runs, error word 0.
- **Routing:** the twin routes in ≥ 3 of the 4 cells; race ≥ 1.03 at T=16/32/128 and ≥ 1.04 at T=8 (block-only, expected 5-7%).
- **Rows:** verify 1 ≤ 81.8, decode 16 ≤ 105.7, decode 32 ≤ 145.2, verify 16 ≤ 234.1 us.
- **Headline:** ≥ 1.92 against today's code level of ~1.90.
- **Scored run:** if ≥ 1.917 (board 1.8941 × 1.012).
stages.fallback:
The twin can only route with a bitwise-clean canary and a race win, so any miss leaves the board's v4/v4c routing in place and the check reads as the board.
- **Races lose:** if every race is < 1.01 while TC1 measured a large stream-K onset excess, the gain did not transfer. Read the [ea4x] staircase line, do not port to decode, and record the lesson.
- **Audit objects to the deferral:** fall back to 'v4x-sync'. It keeps today's mid-stream ticket but uses one thread-0 fence.acq_rel instead of 8 warps' MEMBAR.SC, plus edits 1, 2, 4 and 5. Expected roughly half the gain.

designs.correctness:
BITWISE BY CONSTRUCTION. For every super-group, v4x computes the same per-CTA partials as v4:
- same units, same k order, same acc[bsel] chains;
- same ws slot rule ((sgrp == b/NK) ? 0 : 1, and first_s1 for v4c);
- same contributor set c_first..c_last;
- same fp32 sum: 0.f + p[c_first] + p[c_first+1] + ...;
- same epilogue code (silu_mul and bf16 stores), with gs read from an smem copy of the same floats.

Only which CTA finishes a split super-group, and when, changes. The Map (base, v_e, v_beg, v_n, n_v, n_local, s_cost) is identical, and the 32-bit split equals the 64-bit split within the asserted bounds. So h, y, local_ids and out are bitwise equal to v4 (cw 0) and v4c (cw 7).

MEMORY ORDER
Consumer stores → bar.sync (CTA-scope sync) → thread 0: fence.acq_rel.gpu → relaxed gpu atomics → fence.acq_rel.gpu → bar.sync → every consumer reads partials with __ldcg (L2, no stale L1).
- This forms a PTX release pattern and an acquire pattern, cumulative through bar.sync.
- It is CUTLASS barrier.h GenericBarrier (arrive_inc / wait_eq) and serial split-K.
- The same pattern (barrier, one gpu-scope acq_rel ticket, .cg reload, fixed-order sum, reset) passed on the judge in bf16 (hypotheses/LESSONS.md:48-50).
- Tickets end each launch at 0: the finisher resets them, as today. Flags are per-CTA smem. No spins, so even partially resident grids cannot deadlock (moe's T=256 fork).

CPU EMULATOR (rewrite/bin/ea4x_emul.py, stdlib, run before the audit)
- (E1) Map: the serial thread-0 build and the warp-scan build give equal Maps on ≥ 10,000 cnt vectors, for cw ∈ {0, 6..15}. Edge cases include all-zero, one expert holding 2048 routes, counts of 16k±1, 158 passes, and count < 32.
- (E2) Split: begin_of(c) for c ≤ G, and owner_of(q) for every q, are equal between 64-bit and 32-bit. Space: n_v 1..160, random v_n patterns, NS ∈ {64, 32}, G ∈ {132, 256, 264, 512}, cw ∈ {0, 7, 9, 15}, aligned and stream-K. Plus a bound assertion at the maxima.
- (E3) Protocol: for each configuration, today's protocol and v4x's are simulated under 200 random plus adversarial CTA end orders (heads first, tails first, reversed). Checked:
  - exactly one epilogue per super-group;
  - the finisher's ordered (cta, slot) list equals today's;
  - every partial read was written before the reader's ticket;
  - tickets return to 0.
- (E4) smem: 2·(113,136 + 1,024) ≤ 233,472.
- Negative controls must trip: flip the slot rule, drop a contributor, or skip the reset.
- l3_emul, l4_emul, x1_emul and ea6_emul still pass (consume is untouched).

ON THE JUDGE, before routing
- NaN-poisoned h/y canary, bitwise against the incumbent on every input, twice, error word 0. It covers aligned s=2/4 (4 contributors), stream-K, weighted first_s1, two-tile, zero-local and max-active cases, plus T=128 p10/p50/p90.
- The existing copy checks: graph replays on two states, bitwise.
- The bounded mbarrier waits are unchanged.

FIRST JUDGE RUN: the moe check is the first GPU run of these bytes. Faults stay contained: the twin cannot route without a clean canary, and a twin-module failure leaves the incumbent module, which is a separate .so.
designs.rules:
- **Graph-capturable timed path: holds.** v4x launches exactly like v4 (same grid 264, smem attribute set in prepare, the same PDL attributes, K1 plain). kernel_fn branches only on T and prepare-set state['ea']['on'] / hc['cold_x']. No host syncs, and no allocation from data: buffers are shaped by T as today.
- **Nothing input-derived cached across calls: holds.** Tickets are incremented by every contributor and reset by the finisher inside the same launch, as today. The end-round flags live in per-CTA smem. ws partials are overwritten every call, and the Map is rebuilt per launch from topk_ids.
- **Weights: holds.** Same lossless prepare-time repack (ea["w13r"/"w2r"]); NVFP4 stays NVFP4.
- **fp32 accumulation, bf16 activations: holds.** Identical math.
- **Copy checks replay bitwise, and cross-CTA reductions are order-deterministic: holds.** The finisher sums partials in fixed CTA order whoever finishes. Integer atomics touch tickets only; there are no fp32 atomics on data.

designs.risks:
1. **The fix-up time may not be removable.** It could be mostly store-ack and atomic latency that any correct protocol pays. Then the gain shrinks to the head-stall removal plus map, split and gs (~2-3 us per stream-K call): moe ~+1-1.5%. TC1/TC2 size this tonight, and the per-class race decides routing. TC3 (optional) isolates MEMBAR.SC against acq_rel.
2. **Finish work shifts to the latest-ending CTA.** A CTA may finish 2 super-groups at the kernel tail, about +0.5-1 us on the critical path, against the ~2.5 us head stall removed. Batched loads limit it, and the race measures the net.
3. **Memory-model mistake** in the single-thread release/acquire. That would mean stale partials, rare and non-deterministic. Mitigations: the CUTLASS-proven pattern that has already passed on the judge (LESSONS 48-50); __ldcg reloads; audit focus; a twice-repeated NaN-poisoned bitwise canary; copy checks. designs.title: Engine P: one persistent launch for Engine A at T <= 8 (v6's per-record code, in-kernel h/y counters, fused per-token combine)
designs.angle: Structural (designer 2 of 2). Today Engine A at T=1 (v6pe) and at T=2..8 (v4) runs as three kernels: K1, then K2 (PDL), then the combine. This design replaces those three with one persistent launch, 132 CTAs at 1 CTA/SM. Every CTA runs v6 K1's w13 records and then v6 K2's w2 records through one ring. Two in-kernel integer counters replace the K1->K2 grid boundary and the K2->combine boundary. CTAs 0..T-1 then run ea6_cmb's arithmetic for their token. An exit ticket resets all counters inside the call. Outputs are bitwise equal to v6/v6pe by construction. The engine is raced at prepare against v6pe (T=1) and against v4 (T=2..8). The fixed costs it removes are: K2's restart on a 2-deep ring, K2's lost co-residency at T=8, the PDL grid release, and the combine launch. T=9..16 is out of scope: an all-token B at 16 tokens forces D=2 and two n8 tiles, and loses to v4c on streaming.
designs.summary:
- **What it is.** "EP" is a new kernel eak6::ep_kernel in the v6 module (ea6_kernels.cuh, under `#if EA6_FUSED`). It reuses v6's whole-record geometry:
  - 320 threads: warps 0-7 consume chunk w of each 16-row x 4096-k record, warp 8 streams a 3-deep ring of 36,864-B records, warp 9 sums the 8 partials and writes h/y.
  - CTA c runs v6 K1's flat w13 range [c*512n/G, (c+1)*512n/G), then v6 K2's w2 range of rank a2 = c*n/G, in one record sequence with one ring parity stream.
- **Cross-CTA signals.** These are integer counters only:
  - ctr[a] counts the published w13 records of rank a. Release: every storing lane runs __threadfence, then __syncwarp, then lane 0 does atomicAdd.
  - Before its first w2 record, each consumer warp polls ctr[a2] >= 512 with a volatile ld.global.cg, bounded at 2^26 cycles with err word 2. It then fences and loads h[a2] (T KB per warp) with __ldcg.
  - ctr[32] counts y records. CTAs c < T wait for it to reach 256n, then run ea6_cmb_kernel's body for token c on warps 0-7.
  - ctr[33] is an exit ticket. The last CTA zeroes ctr[0..33].
- **What it removes.**
  - At T=1: K2's restart on its D2=2 ring (anatomy rec2 1.64-1.88 us vs K1's 1.41), the PDL grid release (+0.77 us) and the combine launch.
  - At T=8: also K2's exposed launch, prologue and first fill. v6 K2 cannot co-reside with K1 at T=8 (185,568 + 148,688 B > 228 KB). This stage also removes v4's fix-up/ticket/build_map_t and its three-launch chain; v4's empty block costs 9.3 us in decode.
- **The do-not-try rule rests on a misread.** "No cross-CTA spins" came from the fused bs1 kernel's "bimodal slow mode". Pairing its judge repetitions with SGLang's shows the "slow mode" was simply the judge's n=3 routing draws: ours >= 55 us in exactly the repetitions where SGLang >= 83 us, 59/59, 41/41 and 53/54 in profiles/1105a02a, 7a691942, cd0f6b08. Today's spin-free v6pe board shows the same split: 29 vs 39 us, 56/44 in 0b49b1aa.

  - T=8: about -4.5 us vs v4 (range -2.5 to -7); race wr ~1.07.
  - moe: about +2.0% (1.894 -> ~1.93) from the decode 1 and verify 1 rows.
  - decode: about +0.8% (1.655 -> ~1.67) after the stage-2 port.
- **Stages.**

  - Stage 2 is the decode port on eb-trimd 8cb23d1f.

designs.mechanism:
**1. Decomposition** (`ep_kernel`, T <= 8, grid G = SM count = 132, `__launch_bounds__(320, 1)`, 1 CTA/SM).
- Smem is `smemP(T) = smem6(D13=3, T) + 256`:
  - ring 3 x 36,864;
  - B: 8 chunks x T rows x 1040;
  - P: 8,192;
  - v6's barrier block (bfull left unused);
  - s_n / s_act;
  - red[8][8] for the combine.
  - Totals: 127,624 B at T=1 and 185,824 B at T=8. Both are > 116,736, so exactly one CTA per SM; both are <= 232,448.
- Splits, computed per call from topk_ids (build_map), exactly v6's:
  - w13: R1 = 512n; b1 = c*R1/G, e1 = (c+1)*R1/G in 32-bit (FAST form, exact for n <= 32).
  - w2 (only when n > 0): a2 = c*n/G; c0 = (G*a2+n-1)/n, c1 = (G*(a2+1)+n-1)/n; m = c1-c0, j = c-c0; b2 = 256j/m, e2 = 256(j+1)/m.
  - r1 = e1-b1 >= 3 and r2 = e2-b2 >= 1 for every n >= 1, so no CTA idles. When n == 0: r1 = r2 = 0.
- Record i of the CTA:
  - i < r1 is w13 record q = b1+i. Its source is v6 K1's rec_src (ea6_kernels.cuh:120-125) with NG=128 on w13r; its expert is aa = q/512.
  - i >= r1 is w2 record q = b2+i-r1 of rank a2, NG=64 on w2r.
  - Pieces are at + lane x 18,432, as in v6.

**2. Prologue** (v6 lines 58-88, adapted).
- If (flags & 4), call griddep_wait (decode with PDL; today decode launches plain).
- Consumer warp w stages x rows t < T, chunk w, into B row (w*T+t)*1040: two __ldcg + two st.shared per lane per row. This is FAST's code (L65-72, L181-184) generalized to T rows, and it overlaps warp 0's build_map.
- build_map is called with write_ids=false: EP needs no local_ids.
- Thread 32 initializes full[3], empty[3] (count 8), pfull[2] (8) and pfree[2] (1), then fence_barrier_init, then __syncthreads.

**3. Producer** (warp 8; v6 L126-166 with one sequence).
- For i < r1+r2:
  - slot = i%3;
  - if i >= 3, mbar_wait(empty[slot], ((i/3)-1)&1);
  - lane 0 runs expect_tx(RECB); lanes 0..7 bulk_g2s their piece.
- w2 records are issued as soon as slots free during the last w13 records; they do not depend on h. There is no early return: the warp falls through to the final __syncthreads.

**4. Consumers** (warps 0-7). v6 L189-204 verbatim per record: full wait, eak::consume<2,1>, __syncwarp + empty arrive, pfree wait for i >= 2, P publish, pfull arrive. One addition at i == r1:
```
ctr_wait(ctr + a2, 512, err, dead);           // every lane polls; then __threadfence()
if (threadIdx.x == 0) griddep_launch();       // all CTAs are resident by now: no PDL deadlock
for t < T: B row (w*T+t) <- __ldcg(pin_addr(h + ((size_t)a2*T + t)*4096 + w*512)) (2 uint4 / lane);
__syncwarp();
```
B chunk w is private to warp w (it consumes only chunk w), so overwriting x with h needs no cross-warp barrier.

**5. Epilogue warp** (warp 9).
- Per record: v6 L232-246 (pfull wait, ((p0+p1)+..)+p7 in warp order, pfree arrive).
- i < r1: v6 K1 epilogue L250-260 (h[(aa*T+t)*4096 + col] = bf16(silu_mul(s*gs13[le]))). Count run records of aa. If i == r1-1 or (b1+i+1)/512 != aa, call `ctr_release(ctr + aa, run, lane)` and reset run. That is at most 2 releases per CTA.
- i >= r1: v6 K2 epilogue L262-278 (y rows t*8+s for slots routed to le2 = s_act[a2]; smask computed once, v6 L219-230). After the last record, call `ctr_release(ctr + 32, r2, lane)`.

**6. Combine** (CTAs c < T, warps 0-7, after their record loop). This is ea6_cmb_kernel's body (ea6_kernels.cuh:301-399) with three exact substitutions:
- (a) loc[s] = (unsigned)(topk_ids[c*8+s]-start) < (unsigned)count, instead of ids >= 0. Same value as local_ids.
- (b) `griddep_launch(); griddep_wait();` becomes `ctr_wait(ctr + 32, 256*n, err, dead)`. The w/ids/tw loads stay before it and stay pinned; y is read after it through pin_addr + __ldcg.
- (c) `__syncthreads()` becomes `asm volatile("bar.sync 1, 256;")` (v4's consumer barrier form; only warps 0-7 enter, CTA-uniform).

Output goes to out[c]. With n == 0, the target is 0 and loc[] is all false, so the token gets zeros.

**7. Exit** (in-call reset).
- All warps reach `__syncthreads()`. Then thread 0: `__threadfence(); if (atomicAdd(ctr+33,1) == G-1) { for k<33: ctr[k]=0; __threadfence(); ctr[33]=0; }`.
- Every CTA bumps the ticket only after its last poll and release, so the last arriver's reset races nothing. The next call starts on zeros (kernel boundary).
- ctr is int32[64], allocated with torch.zeros at admission, in state["ea"]. It is per state and cloned by _wg_copy_tree.

**8. Protocol helpers** (new; all instruction forms already ran on the judge: ld.global.cg = __ldcg's LDG.E.STRONG.GPU, MEMBAR from __threadfence, ATOMG.ADD from v1/v4 tickets).
```
__device__ __forceinline__ int ld_cg_v(const int* p){int v;asm volatile("ld.global.cg.s32 %0, [%1];\n":"=r"(v):"l"(p):"memory");return v;}
__device__ __forceinline__ void ctr_wait(const int* p,int target,int* err,bool& dead){
  if(!dead && ld_cg_v(p)<target){const long long t0=clock64();
    while(ld_cg_v(p)<target){if(clock64()-t0>(1ll<<26)){dead=true;if(err)atomicExch(err,2);break;}}}
  __threadfence();}
__device__ __forceinline__ void ctr_release(int* p,int k,int lane){__threadfence();__syncwarp();if(lane==0)atomicAdd(p,k);}
```

**9. Synchronization argument.**
- Every wait targets w13 releases or w2 releases.
- w13 epilogues depend only on their own CTA's ring, consumers and P handshake. A consumer blocked at the transition has already published every w13 P buffer. So the dependency graph is acyclic: w13 -> h-ready -> w2 -> y-ready -> combine -> exit.
- Residency: G = SMs, with occupancy >= 1 asserted at prepare for T=1..8.
  - In moe, EP is the graph's first kernel. In decode it is launched plain after R. All 132 CTAs are therefore resident at once.
  - A dependent launched by PDL can start only after every EP CTA executed launch_dependents, which means after every EP CTA is resident.
  - A broken invariant ends in err word 2 after about 34 ms, never a hang.

**10. Host** (ea6_kernels.cuh tail, `#if EA6_FUSED`).
- `std::vector<int64_t> ep_info()`:
  - sets MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize = smemP(8) and the carveout to max shared;
  - returns ok, numRegs, localSizeBytes, smemP(1), smemP(8), CTAs/SM at smemP(8).
- `void ep_fused(x, topk_ids, tw, nwt, w13r, w2r, gs13, gs2, h, y, out, ctr, err, dbg, T, start, count, grid, flags, eps)`:
  - TORCH_CHECKs: T 1..8; count <= 32; grid 32..1024; ctr int32 >= 34; tw fp32 T*8; nwt bf16 4096; h >= 32*T*4096; y >= 8T*4096; out [T,4096]; 16-B alignment of x, h, y, nwt, out.
  - Launch: cudaLaunchKernelEx with grid x 320, smem smemP(T), and the PDL attribute only if flags & 1.
- dbg (prepare only) holds 12 int64 per CTA: entry, first w13 full, last w13 consume, h staged, first w2 full, last w2 release, combine poll done, combine end, r1, r2, n, last w13 release.

**11. Python (moe, ea6_core.py).**
- `CAMPAIGN_EP` adds `#define EA6_FUSED 1` to the FAST plan entry in `_ea6_build_start`. The fallback build stays the board module.
- `_ep_forward_core`:
  - allocates h [32,T,I], y [8T,H], out [T,H] with torch.empty (scratch accepted);
  - tw32 = topk_weights.to(fp32).contiguous();
  - makes one ext6.ep_fused call with ea["ep_ctr"], grid ea["ea6_grid"] and flags 4 if pdl13.
- Add `_EA6_CORES["ep"]`. moe's _ea_forward dispatches on ea["on"][T].

**12. Gating at prepare** (`_ea6_stage`, after the fc block and before the copy-check loop; every step under EA6_GATE_S / EA6_COPY_S and wrapped like v6).
- **Admission:** EP row ok, lmem 0, occ >= 1 at smemP(1) and smemP(8), SMs x occ >= grid, cmb_ok true.
- **Canary:** `_ea6_canary` gains an "ep" arm at every T=1..8 on v6's inputs, including T=1 forced n=3/4/5, zero-local, max-active and zipf. Scratch is NaN h/y; 2 reps.
  - Pass requires: err word 0; bitwise equal to v6 with the CUDA combine (the v6pe chain at T=1); reps bitwise equal.
  - Report "=v6 bitwise k/k".
- **Class 1:** `_ep_class1` races "ep" vs ea["on"][1] (v6pe) on forced n1..n5 with EA6_W1 weights. Route if wr >= 1.02 in both rounds and every n >= 0.99.
- **Class 8:** `_ep_class8` races "ep" vs ea["on"][8] (v4; the EA_PIN pin only blocks the v1..v6 race) on _ea6_class8's p10/p50/p90 draws. Route if wr >= 1.03 in both rounds and every draw >= 1.00.
- **Anatomy:** `_ep_anatomy` covers T=1 n2 and the T=8 p50 draw, 3 eager runs each.
- **Copy checks:** `_ea6_copy_check(arm="ep")` at T=1 (class 1) and at T=8 and T=2 (class 8).
- **Routing:** set ea["on"][1] and/or ea["on"][2..8] = "ep". PATH lines then read "ENGINE A ep".
- **Log lines:** the [ep] lines go to EA6_LINES, printed last. Drop the v6p/v6s anatomy lines to protect the 14 KB tail.

designs.correctness:
**1. By construction.** EP executes v6's per-record code on identical inputs.
- Same records: piece address = v6 rec_src.
- Same B bytes: x / h rows land at the same B offsets, whether via FAST's __ldcg or v6's bulk copies.
- Same `eak::consume<2,1>` call.
- Same epilogue expressions: the warp-order partial sum, silu_mul, scale and bf16 rounding.
- Same combine expressions: ea6_cmb's body, itself gated bitwise equal to ea_combine (fc canary 10/10, decode 9 inputs x 2).
- Therefore out == v6 + CUDA combine, bitwise, at every T <= 8, and == v6pe at T=1.
- vs v4 at T=2..8 (different k-summation order) the gate is the fp32-reference tolerance. v6 already passes it at T1..8: worst 0.00401 vs master's 0.00862 (0b49b1aa canary).

**2. CPU emulator** (rewrite/bin/ea6_emul.py; local only, exits 0).
- **E1 map:** for n 0..32, T 1..8, G in {132, 114, 128, 144}, EP's per-CTA record sequence:
  - covers every w13 and w2 record of every active rank exactly once;
  - uses piece offsets identical to v6 K1/K2's;
  - writes every h column and y row exactly once, to v6's targets;
  - gives r1 >= 3 and r2 >= 1 for n >= 1;
  - divides by n only when n > 0.
- **E2 releases:** per CTA at most 2 w13 releases. The sum over CTAs is 512 per active rank, and the y-ready total is 256n.
- **E3 multi-CTA protocol.** Reuse `protocol()`'s PTX-parity mbarrier model per CTA. G CTAs x (producer, 8 consumers, epilogue) run with random step order, random lags and random CTA start delays. Counter releases become visible after a random delay, only after the releasing lane's stores. Assert:
  - no deadlock when every CTA eventually starts;
  - each w2 consume of rank a happens after all 512 w13 epilogue stores of a are visible;
  - each combine of token t happens after every y store of its local slots;
  - ring slots and P buffers are never overwritten before use; the parity never aliases;
  - the exit ticket's last arriver leaves ctr all zero, and nothing touches ctr after it;
  - a CTA that never starts makes its group's waits fire (err 2) and the run terminates.
- **E4 fp32 order model:** T4's ea_combine model with loc from topk_ids is bitwise equal to EP's combine, including n_local = 0 (zeros).
- **E5 text:** EP's copied regions (consumer step, both epilogue steps, combine body) are token-equal to ea6_kernel / ea6_cmb_kernel after the three named substitutions.
- **E6 smem:** smemP(1..8) is > 116,736 and <= 232,448 - 1,024. B, P and red are 16-B aligned; barriers 8-B aligned.
- **E7:** --src assembles the module with EA6_FAST and EA6_FUSED and passes `g++ -fsyntax-only` with cuda_stub, with and without the flags.

**3. Prepare gates on the judge** (each failure keeps the incumbent).
- Admission: lmem 0, occupancy, cmb_ok.
- Canary at T1..8 with NaN-poisoned h/y: a missed write or an ordering bug that reads stale h/y shows up as NaN or as not-bitwise. Requires err 0 and 2 reps bitwise.
- Copy checks: graph replays on two states with alternating order, against eager, at T=1, 8 and 2.
- moe's shared `_ea_copy_check` covers every routed engine.
- Decode adds the layer check.
- The judge's own tests run bs 1 and bs 4 on EP when it is routed.

**4. Memory-ordering pattern** (v1/v4's ticket protocol on the boards: ea4_kernels.cuh L306-317):
- releaser: data stores, then __threadfence by every storing lane, then a barrier, then a single atomicAdd;
- observer: sees the count, then __threadfence, then __ldcg reads.
- The only new element is that the observer polls through a volatile asm ld.global.cg, which cannot be hoisted, and the poll is bounded.
designs.rules:
- **CUDA-graph capturable.**
  - One cudaLaunchKernelEx per call. Its arguments are shapes (T), prepare-set tensors and flags; smemP(T) is a shape function.
  - No host sync or allocation from data: torch.empty uses the graph pool.
  - All routing-dependent control (n, s_act, splits, smask, loc) is device-side, as in v6.
  - kernel_fn branches only on T and the prepare-set ea['on'][T].
- **Nothing derived from input data cached across calls.**
  - h, y and out are fully rewritten every call (NaN-scratch canary).
  - Routing metadata is recomputed in-call.
  - The counters are reset inside every timed call by the exit ticket's last CTA. That is deterministic and safe under graph replay, the same pattern as v1/v4's finisher-reset tickets already on both boards.
  - ctr lives per state (cloned by the judge's state copy), so two states never share it.
- **Weights.** Unchanged: v1's lossless prepare-time repack (w13r / w2r records) and gs x 2^7, as v6 uses them.
- **fp32 accumulation, bf16 activations.** MMA accumulators and partial sums are fp32; h and y are bf16 exactly where v6 rounds them; the combine is fp32, then bf16 out.
- **Order-deterministic cross-CTA reductions.** Only integer counters cross CTAs. Every fp32 reduction is intra-CTA in a fixed order: the 8-warp P sum, and the combine's 16-term chains, butterfly and 8-warp sum. There are no fp32 atomics on data. The canary's reps are bitwise and the copy checks replay bitwise.
- **Every key attended.** Not applicable (no attention).
- **All work inside kernel_fn; prepare under 300 s.**
  - Races, anatomy and canaries run only in prepare, on synthetic inputs.
  - +5-8 s build in the existing thread, +10-14 s stage.
  - The anatomy's dbg buffer is prepare-only: kernel_fn passes an empty tensor, which becomes nullptr.
- **No timing patches, harness access, reference import, processes or network.** The diff adds none.
- **Size.** About +21 KB (moe) and +20 KB (decode) against 141 / 77 KB of headroom.
- **Raced against the incumbent at prepare.** Canary vs v6 bitwise, kernel-only race (kernel_fn graphs of the block), copy check. A loss or failure leaves v6pe / v4 routed, and the PATH lines name the routed arm ("ENGINE A ep").
- **No hang or deadlock.**
  - G = SM count with occupancy >= 1 asserted for T=1..8.
  - EP is the graph's first kernel in moe and launched plain after R in decode, so all CTAs are co-resident.
  - The dependency graph is acyclic.
  - launch_dependents runs only after residency.
  - Every poll is bounded (2^26 cycles, err word 2), so a broken invariant gives a failed canary, not a hang.
- **No GPU before the judge.** Correctness comes from construction plus E1-E7 and the audit; the stage-1 check is EP's first GPU run, wrapped like v6's stage.
- **Do-not-try items, and what differs.**
  - "No cross-CTA spins (fused bs1 bimodality)": decode-first nvfp4_engine_forensics.md:146 and :378; LESSONS 2026-10-25 nospin entry; expert_engine_forensics.md:357 ("keep two kernels + PDL").

    - EP still bounds its polls and keeps G = SMs. The check reads runs_ns by baseline mode, so a real spin artifact would be visible.
  - W6-A's "no single-CTA tails" (LOG 2026-10-27T0728Z): EP folds no next-kernel work. Its combine runs on T CTAs, the same parallelism as today's ea6_cmb / ea_combine.
  - fc's rejected ticket-fused K2+combine: no acq_rel PTX is needed, and there is one named barrier (v4's `bar.sync 1, 256` form, CTA-uniform). EP's gain comes from K2's ring restart and K2's lost co-residency at T=8, not from fc's ±0.3 us fusion-only term.

The S1 anatomy prints EP's w13 rec beside v6pe's K1 rec from the same run. An optional CPU SASS opcode census on gpunode06 is possible only if the node may be used (the H100 window is closed; the user's go is needed).

scores.rationale:
It hits the rows that hold the score in both problems: moe T=8/16/32/128 (4 of 6 rows), and decode T=8/16/32 plus the T=128/256 cold half (5 of 6 loads). It is a bitwise twin of the routed engine, so the canary is exact. It has no cross-CTA waits and adds about 30 KB against 130-160 KB of room.

Verified against the sources:
- p3bc.json: the fix-up region takes 11.6/15.2/17.0% of samples, MEMBAR 6.7/8.5/9.7% against 2.3% in the aligned K2, and build_map 4.3-10.4%.
- Decode anatomy in 83f0c00e: 56.4/123.4/131.3 us, with no-route costs of 9.3-9.7 us.
- The ea4_kernels.cuh line references are correct, as are the 32-bit bounds (CT*G = 629,145,600 < 2^31) and the smem budget (2 x 114,160 <= 233,472). The precedent for the acq_rel ticket is LESSONS 48-50.

What the design overstates:
- The '20-21 us fixed cost' assumes a constant cost per pass. Counted as makespan units instead (ceil(W/G) per kernel; K2 aligned at s=1 takes 8 units on n_v*32 CTAs), the T=8/16/32 anatomy fits 2.63 us per unit with intercepts of 9.1 and 13.9 us. That is only 0-5 us above the 9.3 us empty floor.
- K9's 4->5 step is K2's s=2->1 quantization (4 -> 8 units), not a stream-K onset.
- The deferral moves each finish to the latest-ending contributor, so the CTAs with the most units can end on two finishes.

I expect about half of the design's gain: moe +1.5% mid (0.6-2.9) and decode +1.0% (0.4-1.9). P(stage 1 routes with a gain by 06:00Z) is about 0.45.

On today's code (16c33848) the race reads v4 61.7/72.6/104.8 against v6 59.6/74.8/103.7 us, and the v6-pinned judged row read 81.6 against 78.8-79.3 us. UNCHANGED FROM v4 (rewrite/lib/cuda/ea4_kernels.cuh, 509 lines, identical in eb-trim and eb-trimd)
- Unit = (pass of ≤ 16 routes, 128-row super-group, 512-k chunk). K1: NS=64, 512 units per pass. K2: NS=32, 256 units.
- Aligned split when n_v·NS ≤ G, with s = 1/2/4/8. Otherwise stream-K over grid 264 = 2 CTAs/SM × 132. v4c weights the split by cw = pdl bits 4..7.
- Two-record stages (2 × 18,432 B) plus ≤ 16 x/h rows, on a D=2 ring. 8 consumer warps + 1 producer, 288 threads.
- consume / consume2 are untouched: the X1 lesson.

spec.correctness:
BITWISE BY CONSTRUCTION. For every super-group, both arms compute the same per-CTA partials as v4 / v4c:
- the same units, k order and acc chains;
- the same ws slot (the slot rule and first_s1);
- the same contributors c_first..c_last;
- the same fp32 sum 0.f + p[c_first] + p[c_first+1] + ...;
- the same epilogue arithmetic, with gs read from an smem copy of the same floats.
The Map (base, v_e, v_beg, v_n, n_v, n_local, s_cost) is identical, and the 32-bit split equals the 64-bit split inside the asserted bounds. Only which CTA finishes a split super-group, and when, changes (arm d). So h, y, local_ids and out are bitwise equal to the incumbent's.

MEMORY ORDER (both arms)
- Release: consumer stores → bar.sync (CTA scope) → thread 0 fence.acq_rel.gpu → relaxed gpu atomicAdd. This is cumulative over the CTA's stores, as CUTLASS barrier.h states for arrive_inc.
- Acquire: thread 0's atomic result → fence.acq_rel.gpu → bar.sync → every consumer reads the partials with __ldcg (L2, never stale L1).
- The finisher resets the ticket, so tickets are 0 at every launch boundary. Flags live in per-CTA smem.
- No thread ever waits on another CTA, so partially resident grids (moe's T=256 fork) cannot deadlock.
- Same pattern as bf16's split-K ticket that passed on the judge (LESSONS 48-50).

CPU EMULATOR (rewrite/bin/ea4x_emul.py, stdlib, python3 -I, before the audit)
- **E1, Map.** Serial build vs warp-scan build (emulating __shfl_up_sync, where lanes below the offset keep their value): equal Maps on ≥ 10,000 count vectors plus edge cases, cw ∈ {0, 6..15}.
- **E2, split.** 64-bit vs uint32 begin_of / owner_of / cost_of for n_v 1..160, NS 64/32, G sampled in 1..512 (with 132, 160, 192, 255, 256, 264, 512), cw 0/7/9/15, aligned and stream-K, plus no-wrap asserts at the maxima.
- **E3, protocol.** Today's protocol, arm s and arm d under 200 random plus adversarial CTA end orders (heads first, tails first, reversed, max-unit CTAs last). Asserts:
  - one epilogue per super-group;
  - the finisher's ordered (cta, slot) list equals today's;
  - every read partial was stored before its owner's release;
  - tickets end at 0;
  - the fp32 sums of random partials (rounded per add with struct 'f') are bit-equal to today's.
- **E4.** smem and 2-CTA asserts.
- **E5.** --src assembles _ea4x_source() from the generated file and runs g++ -fsyntax-only with rewrite/bin/cuda_stub.
- **Negative controls must trip:** flipped slot rule, dropped contributor, skipped reset, reordered adds, exclusive scan.
- l3_emul, l4_emul, x1_emul and ea6_emul still pass.

ON THE JUDGE, before any route
- Admission: regs, lmem, occupancy.
- NaN-poisoned bitwise canary against the incumbent: 12 T values × every routing kind × both bases × both arms × 2 runs, err 0, tickets 0 after each launch.

- Pin the twins for the final rerun only after ≥ 2 clean judge runs.

- the stream-K fix-up: every consumer thread runs __threadfence (MEMBAR.SC.GPU), then bar, a thread-0 ticket atomic, bar, and a finisher that fences again and loads the partials.

P3b put the fix-up at 11.6-17% of v4 samples and build_map at 4-10%.

A. build_map_x(topk_ids, T, start, count, m, cc, local_ids, write_ids, gs, s_gs, cw)

UNCHANGED FROM v4 (rewrite/lib/cuda/ea4_kernels.cuh, 509 lines, identical in eb-trim and eb-trimd)
- **Decomposition.** Unit = (pass of <= 16 routes, 128-row super-group, 512-k chunk). K1: NS=64 super-groups per pass, 512 units. K2: NS=32, 256 units.
- **Split.** Aligned when n_v*NS <= G, with s = 1/2/4/8; s >= 2 already uses one ws slot and one ticket per CTA. Otherwise stream-K over grid 264 = 2 CTAs/SM x 132. v4c weights the stream-K split by cw = pdl bits 4..7.
- **Pipeline.** Two-record stages (2 x 18,432 B) plus <= 16 x/h rows, on a D=2 ring; 8 consumer warps + 1 producer, 288 threads.
- **Also unchanged:**
  - consume / consume2 (the X1 lesson);
  - PDL placement: K1's early griddep_launch, K2's weight prefetch before griddepcontrol.wait, K1 plain in decode;
  - bounded mbarrier waits with the error word;
  - the ws slot rule ((sgrp == b/NK) ? 0 : 1, and first_s1 for v4c);
  - the contributor sets c_first..c_last;

spec.correctness:
BITWISE BY CONSTRUCTION

For every super-group, both arms compute the same per-CTA partials as v4 / v4c:
- the same units, k order and acc chains;
- the same ws slot (the slot rule and first_s1);
- the same contributors c_first..c_last;
- the same fp32 sum 0.f + p[c_first] + p[c_first+1] + ... (today's per-contributor loop, unchanged);
- the same epilogue arithmetic, with gs read from an smem copy of the same floats;
- the same combine: ea_combine on the board's module, or the Triton one, per cmb_t[T].

The Map (base, v_e, v_beg, v_n, n_v, n_local, s_cost) is identical, and the 32-bit split equals the 64-bit split inside the asserted bounds. Only which CTA finishes a split super-group, and when, changes (arm d). So h, y, local_ids and out are bitwise equal to the incumbent's.

MEMORY ORDER (both arms; CUTLASS GenericBarrier's arrive_inc / wait)
- **Release:** consumer stores -> bar.sync (CTA scope) -> thread 0 fence.acq_rel.gpu -> relaxed gpu atomicAdd. This is cumulative over the CTA's stores.
- **Acquire:** thread 0's atomic result -> fence.acq_rel.gpu (only when this CTA finishes) -> bar.sync -> every consumer reads the partials with __ldcg (L2; today's finisher loads are LDG.E.128.STRONG.GPU).
- **Tickets:** the finisher resets its ticket, so tickets are 0 at every launch boundary. Flags live in per-CTA smem, and pend is CTA-uniform.
- **No cross-CTA waits:** no thread ever waits on another CTA, so partially resident grids (moe's T=256 fork) cannot deadlock. Only bar_consumers is used after the producer warp returns.
- Same pattern as bf16's split-K ticket that passed on the judge (LESSONS 48-50).

MODULES
- The twins' kernels come from ea['ext4x']; the combine always comes from ea['ext'] (ea3_core.py 24 / 44).
- E6 checks this statically. Admission also checks hasattr for every _EA4X_FNS name, and for ea['ext'].ea_combine whenever any cmb_t is set.

CPU EMULATOR (rewrite/bin/ea4x_emul.py, stdlib, python3 -I, before the audit)
- **E1, Map.** Serial build against the warp-scan build (emulating __shfl_up_sync, where lanes below the offset keep their value): equal Maps on >= 10,000 count vectors plus edge cases, cw in {0, 6..15}.
- **E2, split.** 64-bit against uint32 begin_of / owner_of / cost_of for n_v 1..160, NS 64/32, G sampled in 1..512 (including 132, 160, 192, 255, 256, 257, 260, 264, 512), cw 0/7/9/15, aligned and stream-K, plus no-wrap asserts at the maxima.
- **E3, protocol.** Today's protocol, arm s and arm d under 200 random plus adversarial CTA end orders (heads first, tails first, reversed, max-unit CTAs last). Asserts:
  - exactly one epilogue per super-group;
  - the finisher's ordered (cta, slot) list equals today's;
  - every read partial was stored before its owner's release;
  - tickets end at 0;

0. WHAT AND WHY

Engine A v4 / v4c (rewrite/lib/cuda/ea4_kernels.cuh, namespace eak4) is the routed NVFP4 expert block for:
- moe T=2..32 and T=128;
- decode T=2..32, plus the cold half at T=128/256.

Besides streaming weights, each launch pays fixed work:
- thread 0's serial 32-expert pass-list loop in build_map_t (lines 102-116) and, for v4c, a second thread-0 cost loop (169-182);
- 64-bit split math (183-209);
- a global gs[le] load in every epilogue;
- stream-K fix-ups. At each partial super-group's end, all 256 consumer threads run __threadfence (MEMBAR.SC.GPU), then a barrier, a thread-0 ticket atomic and another barrier; the last arriver fences again and sums the partials. Every stream-K CTA has a head partial, which stalls the stream mid-way, and a tail partial at its end.

Evidence:
- P3b (H100 ncu) put the fix-up region at 11.6-17% of v4 samples and build_map at 4-10%.
- On the H200, K1's aligned -> stream-K step costs about 2.6 us more than its units predict (a7a013ba).

You build v4x: a SEPARATE module of twin kernels whose outputs are BITWISE equal to v4 / v4c, in two arms:
- **Arm d (the bet):** each partial super-group's ticket is deferred to one round at the CTA's end, so the head partial no longer stalls the stream. The tail round and the finish stay.
- **Arm s (control):** today's schedule, with a single-thread fence around the ticket instead of 256 threads' MEMBAR.SC. Expected gain is about 0; it is raced only to separate the effects. It may route if it wins on its own, but no gain is booked for it and it is never shipped alone.

Both arms also get a warp-scan pass list, 32-bit split math and gs in smem.

Each class races the incumbent against both arms at prepare time. A twin routes only when it is admitted, bitwise canary-clean, faster, and clean in its own copy check.

These stay byte-identical: the board's Engine A module (_EA2_SRC), v6 and the combine. The combine is ALWAYS called on the board's module (ea['ext']), never on the twin module.

Expected (mid): moe +1.1% (verify 1 -1.0 us; decode 16 / decode 32 / verify 16 -2.6 us each), with a range of +0.4% to +2.3%.
